name: Dependency Confusion (Public-Registry Name Squatting)
description: Supply-chain attack where a package name used only by an organization's INTERNAL registry is also published to the PUBLIC registry (npm/PyPI/RubyGems/etc.) with a higher version number. Build tooling that queries both registries and picks the highest version then pulls the attacker's package, executing attacker code (install scripts) inside the victim's build/CI. Covers name discovery, higher-version squatting, and exfil via install hooks.
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  Package managers often resolve a name across BOTH an internal/private registry and the public registry, then install the HIGHEST version available. If an internal-only name is unregistered publicly, an attacker publishes it publicly with a huge version (e.g. 99.0.0) and the build pulls it.

=== FIND INTERNAL NAMES ===
  - Leaked package.json / requirements.txt / *.csproj / build logs in public repos, JS bundles, error pages, Docker images.
  - Internal scoped names without a reserved public scope (@company/foo where the @company scope is unclaimed on npm).

=== NPM PoC PACKAGE ===
  package.json:
    { "name": "internal-logger", "version": "99.0.0", "scripts": { "preinstall": "node exfil.js" } }
  exfil.js sends hostname/env/whoami to a collaborator URL (DNS/HTTP out of the build network).
  npm publish --registry https://registry.npmjs.org --access public

=== PYPI ===
  - setup.py with code in setup() runs on install; publish with a higher version than the internal one.
  - twine upload dist/*

=== SAFE PoC ===
  - Use ONLY a canary beacon (hostname + a unique token to a Burp Collaborator / interactsh domain). Do not exfil secrets or run destructive code; this is lab-only / authorized research.

=== DEFENDER NOTE ===
  This is a supply-chain primitive; the 'attack' happens inside the victim's build, so detection lives in CI egress + registry policy, not web logs.

Secret/name discovery in public repos surfaces internal package names.

defense.why_it_works: Package managers that query a public registry alongside a private one and select the highest semantic version will prefer an attacker's public package when an internal-only name is unclaimed publicly. Install-time scripts then execute in the build.
defense.prerequisites: An internal package name that is NOT reserved on the public registry, plus a build configuration that does not pin the registry/scope or lock hashes.
defense.impact: Arbitrary code execution inside CI/CD or developer machines, theft of build secrets and source, and a foothold for broader supply-chain compromise of shipped artifacts.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1195.001] CI build egress to package registries resolving internal names from the PUBLIC registry, install-script child processes spawning network/exec, and unexpected version jumps (e.g. 99.0.0) for internal packages.
defense.artifacts: CI/CD build logs (resolved registry URL and version per dependency), egress proxy logs from build runners, npm/pip audit output, and registry access logs showing public fetches of internal names.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=proxy src_category=ci_runner (uri_host="registry.npmjs.org" OR uri_host="pypi.org")
| rex field=uri_path "/(?<pkg>[^/]+)"
| search pkg IN (internal_pkg_list)
| stats count by src_ip, pkg, uri_host
defense.elastic_kql: destination.domain:("registry.npmjs.org" or "pypi.org") and source.labels.role:"ci-runner" and url.path:*internal*
defense.sentinel_kql:
CommonSecurityLog
| where DeviceEventClassID == "proxy" and RequestURL has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","pypi.org")
| where SourceUserName == "ci-runner"
| summarize count() by SourceIP, RequestURL
defense.prevention: Reserve all internal package names/scopes on the public registries. Pin builds to the private registry only (scoped registry config, no public fallback), enforce lockfiles with integrity hashes, use .npmrc/pip index-url that forbids public resolution of internal names, and disable or sandbox install scripts (npm --ignore-scripts).

detections.name: CI runner fetching an internal package name from a public registry
detections.logic:
index=proxy (uri_host="registry.npmjs.org" OR uri_host="pypi.org")
| rex field=uri_path "/(?<pkg>[a-zA-Z0-9@._-]+)"
| lookup internal_packages name AS pkg OUTPUT name AS is_internal
| where isnotnull(is_internal)
| stats count values(uri_path) by src_ip, pkg
detections.false_positives: An internal name that is also a legitimate public package (verify ownership).
detections.tuning: Maintain a lookup of internal package names; alert only when a build runner resolves one against the public registry.
